sources.ref_file_title: Ale03 - More on average case vs approximation complexity
sources.note: Abstract states: 'There exists a secure public-key (probabilistic) cryptosystem, based on the intractability of decoding of random binary codes.' Alekhnovich states his assumptions as conjectures about decoding random binary codes at noise weight ~sqrt(n); the LPN(eps = Theta(1/sqrt(k))) formulation is the standard modern restatement.

pages.class_justification: One fixed construction whose public key and ciphertexts are noisy codewords of random linear codes sampled from the LPN distribution; the security proof is a hybrid argument replacing key and challenge ciphertext by uniform strings under decisional LPN, invoking the IND-CPA adversary only as a distinguisher oracle. This is the standard fully-black-box shape.
pages.model_justification: Plain-model construction; no idealized oracle or setup.
pages.statement: Hardness of decisional [[learning-parity-with-noise|LPN]] at noise rate $\varepsilon = \Theta(1/\sqrt{k})$ — the $\gamma = 1/2$ point of the [[learning-parity-with-noise#noise-level|mid-noise]] regime — implies IND-CPA-secure [[public-key-encryption|PKE]] — [[Ale03 - More on average case vs approximation complexity|Ale03]]. Hardness at any lower noise rate, in particular the low-noise regime $\varepsilon = \log^c(k)/k$, implies hardness at $\Theta(1/\sqrt{k})$ by re-randomizing the noise, so the same conclusion follows.
pages.sketch: The receiver's secret is a sparse noise vector of weight $\Theta(\sqrt{m})$ planted in a random linear code; a ciphertext embeds a fresh noisy codeword with independent weight-$\Theta(\sqrt{m})$ noise. Two independent such vectors overlap in $O(1)$ positions in expectation, so their inner product is biased toward $0$, letting the receiver recover the encrypted bit with noticeable advantage; an outer error-correcting code amplifies correctness, and decisional-LPN hybrids replace key and ciphertext by uniform.
flags: Hypothesis id lpn-mid-noise covers the whole 1/k^gamma family; Ale03 needs only the gamma = 1/2 instance (eps = Theta(1/sqrt(k))). Note the literature usually calls this regime 'low-noise LPN', which collides with this wiki's stricter 'low-noise' (log^c(k)/k) label — the statement pins the concrete rate to avoid the clash.

Duplicate edge: content/Reductions/lpn-to-pke.md (red-lpn-to-pke, batch red-18) records the same claim ('PKE can be built assuming Mid-noise LPN') with hypothesis plain lpn and no citation; the two pages should be merged with this one (which carries the citation and the noise-regime hypothesis) as the survivor.

sources.ref_file_title: LMW23 - Doubly Efficient Private Information Retrieval and Fully Homomorphic RAM Computation from Ring LWE
sources.authors: Wei-Kai Lin, Ethan Mook, Daniel Wichs
sources.note: STOC 2023 best paper. Abstract: unkeyed DEPIR with deterministic preprocessing, security under the standard RingLWE assumption; preprocessing time/size O(N^{1+eps}), per-query time and communication polylog(N), updates in O(N^eps).

pages.class_justification: LMW23 do not classify the reduction, and the conclusion carries efficiency requirements (doubly efficient server time) beyond a security property, so the RTV axes do not apply cleanly. Left unstated rather than guessed.
pages.model_justification: Plain model; the preprocessing is deterministic and public, with no random oracle or common setup.
pages.statement: Hardness of [[learning-with-errors#ring-lwe|Ring-LWE]] implies unkeyed [[doubly-efficient-pir|DEPIR]]: for every constant $\varepsilon > 0$, the server deterministically preprocesses a size-$N$ database in time and space $O(N^{1+\varepsilon})$, after which each query is answered in $\polylog(N)$ time and communication — [[LMW23 - Doubly Efficient Private Information Retrieval and Fully Homomorphic RAM Computation from Ring LWE|LMW23]]. The preprocessed database supports updates in time $O(N^{\varepsilon})$.
pages.sketch: LMW23 first build a PIR in which the server's entire computation is evaluating a fixed multivariate polynomial: the database is encoded as a low-degree polynomial and the query is a Ring-LWE-based somewhat-homomorphic encryption of the index point whose homomorphic evaluation is literal polynomial evaluation over a ring. Preprocessing that polynomial with the Kedlaya–Umans fast polynomial-evaluation data structure (STOC 2008) makes each online evaluation polylogarithmic.
notes_to_keep: LMW23 also constructs fully homomorphic RAM computation from Ring-LWE — a second conclusion with no object page of its own.
flags: Frontmatter hypothesis should be ring-lwe, not lwe: the LMW23 result is proved under RingLWE specifically (the paper's title and abstract say so), and the LWE page defines ring-lwe as a variant id. Plain LWE is not known to yield DEPIR.
The migrated bullet writes the storage bound in N and the online bound in n; the abstract states both in N — use N throughout.

sources.ref_file_title: LMW24 - Doubly Efficient Cryptography Commitments, Arguments and RAM MPC
sources.authors: Wei-Kai Lin, Ethan Mook, Daniel Wichs
sources.note: Abstract: doubly efficient commitments, arguments and RAM MPC in the plain model without common setup; parties preprocess inputs offline and then run many executions in sublinear online time; constructions rely on DEPIR as a building block and are instantiated from Ring LWE.

pages.class_justification: LMW24 do not classify the reduction, and the conclusion bundles efficiency (sublinear online time) with security, outside the RTV axes. Left unstated.
pages.model_justification: Plain model, explicitly without any common setup.
pages.statement: Hardness of [[learning-with-errors#ring-lwe|Ring-LWE]] implies [[doubly-efficient-ram-mpc|doubly efficient RAM-MPC]] in the plain model: each party preprocesses its input once, offline, after which any number of MPC executions over those inputs run in online time sublinear in the input size — [[LMW24 - Doubly Efficient Cryptography Commitments, Arguments and RAM MPC|LMW24]]. The same work obtains doubly efficient commitments and succinct arguments in which the committer and prover run in sublinear online time.
pages.sketch: The parties preprocess their inputs into databases of the unkeyed DEPIR of LMW23, so the protocol can make privacy-preserving sublinear-time accesses to them; Ring-LWE instantiates both the DEPIR and the remaining cryptographic components.
notes_to_keep: The conclusion object doubly-efficient-ram-mpc has no wiki page (closest existing page is doubly-efficient-pir).
flags: Frontmatter hypothesis should be ring-lwe, not lwe: LMW24's constructions are instantiated from Ring LWE (via the LMW23 DEPIR); plain LWE is not known to suffice.

The edge factors through DEPIR: LMW24 explicitly builds on DEPIR as its main building block, so a cleaner split is ring-lwe => depir (red-lwe-to-depir-lmw23) plus a depir => de-ram-mpc edge citing LMW24; the current page compresses the chain.

The correct hyperedge already exists as content/Reductions/module-lwe-and-module-sis-to-ds.md (red-module-lwe-and-module-sis-to-ds), which should cite Lyubashevsky's Fiat-Shamir-with-aborts line (Lyu09/Lyu12) or the CRYSTALS-Dilithium design paper (DKL+18) rather than LS15. If the module edge is fleshed out, its model must be rom (Fiat-Shamir with aborts); QROM security is a separate, stronger claim.

sources.ref_file_title: Reg05 - On Lattices, Learning with Errors, Random Linear Codes, and Cryptography
sources.note: Reg05 gives the IND-CPA PKE; viewing it as a KEM (encapsulate a uniformly random session key) is immediate and standard.

pages.class_justification: Composition of Regev's fixed construction with the generic PKE-to-KEM step (encrypt a random session key). The security reduction runs the KEM adversary once as an oracle to break IND-CPA of the underlying PKE and hence decision LWE — the standard fully-black-box shape.
pages.model_justification: Regev's scheme and the PKE-to-KEM step need no idealized oracle. (The FO transform mentioned in the migrated Kyber quote is a ROM result, but it belongs to a different edge.)
pages.statement: Hardness of decision [[learning-with-errors|LWE]] implies an [[key-encapsulation-mechanism#ind-cpa-kem|IND-CPA KEM]]: encapsulation encrypts a uniformly random session key under Regev's LWE encryption scheme — [[Reg05 - On Lattices, Learning with Errors, Random Linear Codes, and Cryptography|Reg05]].
pages.sketch: Regev's PKE is IND-CPA under decision LWE; encapsulating a uniformly random key with it yields an IND-CPA KEM, since a distinguisher between the encapsulated key and a fresh random key contradicts IND-CPA of the encryption.
flags: Redundant composite: this edge equals red-lwe-to-pke-reg05 composed with red-pke-to-kem (both exist as pages). Under the one-page-per-link rule, consider deleting this page rather than keeping a parallel compressed chain.

The migrated quote is entirely about Kyber / ML-KEM: hypothesis Module-LWE (not plain LWE), conclusion IND-CCA via the Fujisaki-Okamoto transform in the ROM. That content belongs on red-module-lwe-to-kem and red-ind-cpa-kem-to-ind-cca-security, not here.

sources.ref_file_title: BGV12 - Leveled fully homomorphic encryption without bootstrapping
sources.authors: Zvika Brakerski, Craig Gentry, Vinod Vaikuntanathan

sources.ref_file_title: GSW13 - Homomorphic Encryption from Learning with Errors Conceptually-Simpler, Asymptotically-Faster, Attribute-Based
sources.authors: Craig Gentry, Amit Sahai, Brent Waters
sources.note: Also eprint 2013/340. Approximate-eigenvector method; no evaluation key.

pages.class_justification: One fixed construction; the hypothesis is an assumption and the security proof is a sequence of hybrids over the acyclic chain of key-switching hints (encryptions of level-i key material under the level-(i-1) key), each step converting the IND-CPA adversary, used only as an oracle, into a decision-LWE distinguisher.
pages.model_justification: Plain-model construction; the point of the leveled scheme is that it needs neither bootstrapping nor a circular-security assumption.
pages.statement: For every depth bound $L$ fixed at key generation, hardness of decision [[learning-with-errors|LWE]] (at a modulus-to-noise ratio growing with $L$) yields [[homomorphic-encryption#leveled-fully-homomorphic-encryption|leveled FHE]] evaluating all polynomial-size circuits of depth $L$, with no bootstrapping and no circular-security assumption — [[BGV12 - Leveled fully homomorphic encryption without bootstrapping|BGV12]].
pages.sketch: Ciphertexts are Regev-style LWE encryptions under a ladder of moduli $q_L > \cdots > q_0$; each homomorphic multiplication is followed by key switching back to a canonical secret and modulus switching one rung down the ladder, which keeps the noise-to-modulus ratio under control so depth $L$ is reached without bootstrapping.
pages.improvements_text: - The approximate-eigenvector method gives leveled FHE from LWE with no evaluation key and no key or modulus switching; homomorphic addition and multiplication are just matrix addition and multiplication — [[GSW13 - Homomorphic Encryption from Learning with Errors Conceptually-Simpler, Asymptotically-Faster, Attribute-Based|GSW13]]
flags: BGV12 also gives a Ring-LWE instantiation with better efficiency; the plain-LWE hypothesis recorded here is correct for the main theorem.

Prior work BV11 (Brakerski-Vaikuntanathan, FOCS 2011) built (somewhat/leveled-with-bootstrapping) FHE from standard LWE first; BGV12's contribution is leveled FHE without bootstrapping. The migrated 'first efficient construction from LWE' gloss elides this — not preserved in the statement.

sources.ref_file_title: Reg05 - On Lattices, Learning with Errors, Random Linear Codes, and Cryptography

pages.class_justification: One fixed construction using only samples of the LWE distribution; the security proof runs any IND-CPA adversary once, as an oracle, inside a two-step hybrid: decision LWE replaces the public key by uniform, after which the leftover hash lemma makes the challenge ciphertext statistically independent of the bit. Any advantage difference is a decision-LWE distinguisher.
pages.model_justification: Plain-model construction. (Reg05's separate worst-case hardness theorem for LWE is a quantum reduction, but that is a different edge: red-gapsvp-to-lwe-reg05 / red-sivp-to-lwe-reg05.)
pages.statement: Hardness of decision [[learning-with-errors|LWE]] for $(n, q, \chi, m)$ with $m = O(n \log q)$ implies IND-CPA-secure [[public-key-encryption|PKE]]: the public key is $m$ LWE samples, and a bit $\mu$ is encrypted as a random subset-sum of the samples plus $\mu \lfloor q/2 \rfloor$ — [[Reg05 - On Lattices, Learning with Errors, Random Linear Codes, and Cryptography|Reg05]].
pages.sketch: $\KeyGen$ outputs $\pk = (\mathbf{A}, \mathbf{b} = \mathbf{A}\mathbf{s} + \mathbf{e})$ and $\sk = \mathbf{s}$; $\Enc(\pk, \mu)$ samples $\mathbf{r} \getsr \bits^m$ and outputs $(\mathbf{r}^{\top}\mathbf{A},\ \mathbf{r}^{\top}\mathbf{b} + \mu \lfloor q/2 \rfloor)$; $\Dec(\sk, (\mathbf{c}_1, c_2))$ computes $c_2 - \langle \mathbf{c}_1, \mathbf{s} \rangle = \mathbf{r}^{\top}\mathbf{e} + \mu \lfloor q/2 \rfloor$ and rounds. Security: decision LWE replaces $(\mathbf{A}, \mathbf{b})$ by uniform, and then $(\mathbf{r}^{\top}\mathbf{A}, \mathbf{r}^{\top}\mathbf{b})$ is statistically close to uniform by the leftover hash lemma, so the ciphertext hides $\mu$.
flags: The migrated key-exchange bullet (KE from LWE 'as a special case of PKE from LWE') is the composite lwe => pke => ke; the second link is the existing red-pke-to-ke page and should not be re-recorded here.
The 'security rooted in worst-case lattice hardness' clause is the separate worst-case edge (red-gapsvp-to-lwe-reg05 / red-sivp-to-lwe-reg05), already recorded.

pages.wrong_reason: Misattributed hypothesis. CG24's pseudorandom codes rest on either 2^{O(sqrt(n))}-hardness of LPN, or polynomial hardness of LPN together with the planted-XOR problem at low density — verified against the paper's abstract (CRYPTO 2024; eprint 2024/235). No construction in CG24 is based on LWE; follow-up work (Christ et al., 'Improved Pseudorandom Codes from Permuted Puzzles', 2025) explicitly lists PRCs from LWE as an open question. The correct edge already exists as content/Reductions/subexponential-lpn-to-prc-cg24.md. The source-prose bullet ('the LWE ciphertext structure naturally yields a pseudorandom, decodable code') appears to be invented; the page's own Notes already flag the suspicion.
flags: Sibling page content/Reductions/lwe-to-zero-bit-prc-cg24.md (batch red-20) shares the same misattribution, including a parameter claim (n = O(secpar^2/log secpar)) that does not correspond to anything in CG24 — flag to that batch's verifier.
The originating bullets on content/Primitives/pseudorandom-error-correcting-code.md should be corrected to LPN-based hypotheses in the same pass.

sources.ref_file_title: DGI+19 - Trapdoor Hash Functions and Their Applications
sources.authors: Nico Döttling, Sanjam Garg, Yuval Ishai, Giulio Malavolta, Tamer Mour, Rafail Ostrovsky
sources.note: Abstract: 'We obtain constructions where the hint is only one bit long based on DDH, QR, DCR, or LWE.'

pages.class_justification: DGI+19 do not classify the reduction. The security reduction is a direct embedding of an LWE challenge into the encoding key and is very likely fully-black-box, but the paper does not say so and the correctness analysis (rounding-error handling) was not verified here — left unstated.
pages.statement: Hardness of decision [[learning-with-errors|LWE]] implies [[trapdoor-hash-function|TDH]] with one-bit hints: for every index $i$ one can sample an encoding key hiding $i$, together with a trapdoor that recovers the input bit $x_i$ from the hash $H(x)$ and a single hint bit — [[DGI+19 - Trapdoor Hash Functions and Their Applications|DGI+19]].
pages.sketch: The hash of $x$ is $\mathbf{A}x$ for a public matrix $\mathbf{A}$; the encoding key for index $i$ is an LWE-style encryption of the $i$-th unit vector, and the hint is a rounded inner product of that encryption with $x$. Knowing the LWE secret and $H(x) = \mathbf{A}x$, the trapdoor holder determines which value of $x_i$ is consistent with the hint, up to small rounding error; index privacy is exactly LWE pseudorandomness of the encoding key.
notes_to_keep: The sub-bullet's claim that TDH generically yields PIR is an independent edge (TDH ⇒ PIR, DGI+19) that is not yet recorded.
flags: DGI+19 also construct TDH from DDH, QR, and DCR. Sibling edges exist for DDH (red-ddh-to-tdh-dgi-19) and QR (red-qr-to-tdh-dgi-19), but a dcr-to-tdh-dgi-19 edge appears to be missing.
The migrated quote records only the PIR application; the DGI+19 TDH => PIR link deserves its own reduction page (distinct from the existing red-tdh-to-cpir-amr25, which cites AMR25).
